title: Salary Sacrifice Meaning: How It Affects Your Hourly to Annual Pay Conversion
description: Understand salary sacrifice meaning and how it impacts your hourly to annual pay calculation. Learn about 38-hour weeks, tax, super, and award rates with our guide.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year, before tax, super, or salary sacrifice.

faqs.q: What is salary sacrifice meaning in the context of hourly to annual pay?
faqs.a: Salary sacrifice meaning refers to an arrangement where you agree to forgo part of your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits such as additional superannuation contributions, a car, or other non-cash benefits. This reduces your taxable income but also lowers the ordinary earnings base used for super guarantee calculations. When converting hourly to annual pay, salary sacrifice can alter the effective gross figure because the sacrificed amount is not counted as cash salary, though it may still be included in total remuneration. Our calculator assumes no salary sacrifice, so you should adjust your hourly rate if you have such an arrangement.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of leave entitlements. If you are a casual employee, your annual pay is calculated using the loaded rate (base rate × 1.25) multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks. For example, the National Minimum Wage for casuals from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour including loading. Our calculator has a checkbox to add casual loading automatically; do not type a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement, set by the Fair Work Commission at $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. Award rates are industry- or occupation-specific minimums set by the Fair Work Ombudsman, which are often higher than the national minimum. Your actual pay may be determined by an award, enterprise agreement, or individual contract. Our reference tables provide averages, not job-specific medians.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross salary using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

To see your fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. Weekly pay is your hourly rate times your weekly hours. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, weekly pay is $1,140 and fortnightly pay is $2,280. This can help you budget or compare with salary offers that are quoted per year or per fortnight.

### When to Use 38 Hours

The 38-hour week is the standard for full-time employment under the National Employment Standards. However, part-time or casual employees may work fewer or irregular hours. Our calculator on [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your own hours per week. If you are unsure, 38 hours is a safe assumption for full-time work. Always check your award or agreement for your ordinary hours.

## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour**, which equates to $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. If you are a casual employee, you receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

Award rates are higher than the national minimum for many industries and occupations. For example, the Hospitality Award or the General Retail Industry Award have specific pay rates for different classifications. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) that list these rates. Our [reference tables](/data) include averages from the Australian Bureau of Statistics, such as the May 2026 Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time ($2,083.70 per week) and all employees total earnings ($1,579.20 per week). These are averages, not medians for a specific job.

**Important:** Do not confuse the National Minimum Wage or award rates with a job median. Our site does not provide job-specific medians. If you see an industry average, it is an average, not the median for your role.

## The Role of Superannuation

Superannuation is a compulsory contribution your employer must pay on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is **12% of your ordinary earnings**, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means if your annual gross is $100,000, your employer adds $12,000 to your super fund, making total remuneration $112,000. Super is paid on top, not deducted from your hourly rate.

### Salary Sacrifice Meaning and Super

Salary sacrifice meaning is an arrangement where you agree to reduce your pre-tax salary in exchange for benefits, most commonly additional super contributions. For example, you might sacrifice $10,000 of your salary into super. This reduces your taxable income but also lowers the ordinary earnings base for the super guarantee (though the sacrificed amount still receives the 12% contribution from your employer if it is part of your ordinary earnings). Understanding salary sacrifice meaning is crucial when converting hourly to annual pay because the sacrificed amount is not cash you receive, but it still forms part of your total remuneration package. Our calculator assumes no salary sacrifice, so if you have one, adjust your hourly rate to reflect the cash component only.

## Tax and Medicare

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Our tax estimate uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide. Salary sacrifice can reduce your taxable income, potentially lowering your tax bracket. For more details on tax and super, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) pages.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) calculator lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then shows your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. Remember:
- Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; use the checkbox instead.
- The annual figure is hourly × hours per week × 52.
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base.
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold.
- No deductions for HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

For more information, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page, [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide, or [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data. If you need to convert a salary offer to hourly, use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool. And if you want to understand how your job compares to industry averages, check [job pay](/topics/job-pay).

## Disclaimer

This guide provides estimates only. Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is not a determination of your actual pay or tax liability. Always consult a qualified professional for your specific circumstances.
